source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify one person to blame, without examining organizational exposure or safer-system changes after the event.","B":"Replace clinical quality-improvement teams, because legal and financial risk review makes clinical investigation unnecessary.","C":"Assess organizational risk and support event response, documentation, disclosure processes, and prevention planning.","D":"Limit involvement to insurance billing, because adverse-event investigation and disclosure fall outside risk management work."}}
source_row.rationale: Risk management participates in a coordinated adverse-event response that includes investigation, disclosure/risk evaluation and corrective action with clinical, quality and leadership functions rather than serving only as a blame-assignment office.
source_row.source_detail: CANDOR framework integrates event investigation, communication/disclosure, patient/family engagement, caregiver support and resolution across organizational clinical, quality, risk and leadership functions. Current AHRQ CANDOR Toolkit module rechecked 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: AHRQ — CANDOR Response and Disclosure Framework
source_row.stem: After a serious adverse event, what is an appropriate role for hospital risk management within a coordinated response?
